bibliography.abstract: Deployed tourism trip planners ingest travel times and ratings as exact numbers, although routing services return travel times that vary with the hour of departure and a platform rating may rest on a handful of reviews or on tens of thousands. We present an eco-friendly trip planner that represents both quantities as Z-numbers, which pair a fuzzy restriction on a value with a fuzzy reliability on the evidence behind it, and that constructs them directly from routing-service observations at six departure hours and from platform review counts rather than from linguistic elicitation. A hybrid loss combines score, carbon, travel-time, and reliability terms, and an adaptive large neighborhood search returns single-day itineraries with per-leg reliability annotations through a conversational front end. We compare the planner with a crisp-mean baseline under an identical optimizer in Baku, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Tashkent, and Istanbul, with fifteen points of interest and thirty seeds per city, and we evaluate the selected itineraries on their trip carbon and their total travel time. Pooled over 150 seed-paired runs, the planner lowers trip carbon from 3.24 to 2.61 kg (19.3%, Wilcoxon p = 0.017; city-clustered bootstrap interval 6.4% to 26.7%) and travel time from 123 to 109 minutes per trip (11.5%, p = 2.8e-10; interval 5.0% to 18.2%). The travel-time reductions survive a Holm correction in Baku, Istanbul, and Abu Dhabi, the carbon reduction is significant in Baku and large but uncertain in the dispersed catalogs of Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and neither metric changes in Tashkent. Review counts were measured for Baku and estimated for the other four cities, and the comparison involves a single baseline, so the results establish feasibility and direction rather than a general advantage. Code, routing caches, frozen routing tables, and per-seed results are openly released.

bibliography.title: An Eco-Friendly Tourism Trip Planner Driven by Z-Number Uncertainty: Evidence from Baku, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Tashkent, and Istanbul

en.caveats: Because all evaluated points of interest had over 3,000 reviews, rating reliability remained uniform across the sample, and performance improvements varied substantially by city spatial structure.
en.what: This paper developed an eco-friendly tourism itinerary generator that models travel times and user ratings using Z-numbers derived from departure-hour routing data and total review counts. Using an adaptive large neighborhood search algorithm, the authors benchmarked the system against a crisp-mean planner across 15 points of interest in Baku, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Tashkent, and Istanbul over 150 seed-paired runs. The proposed method reduced average trip carbon emissions by 19.3% (from 3.24 to 2.61 kg) and total travel time by 11.5% (from 123 to 109 minutes).
en.why: It replaces exact-value assumptions in travel recommendation systems with uncertainty-aware fuzzy reliability, establishing that accounting for travel-time variance and rating volume directly lowers carbon emissions and transit duration.
